Number to Words Converter

Fast tools that run in your browser. No login, no sign-up.

Everything runs in your browser. Your text and files are not uploaded to our servers. No account or login is needed.

How to use

  1. Type a number, for example 1234.56. Spaces and thousands separators are accepted.
  2. Choose the output language and, if you like, a letter case and a currency or unit word.
  3. The words appear as you type. Press Copy to take them.

About this tool

Converts a number into words in English, Spanish, Portuguese, Indonesian, Hindi or Arabic. It handles whole numbers up to 15 digits, decimals (read digit by digit), negative numbers and an optional currency or unit word, for example “one hundred twenty-three rupiah”. Choose lowercase, sentence case, Title Case or UPPERCASE, and tick the British option to add “and” in English (one hundred and twenty-three). Spanish uses the long scale (mil millones, billón), Portuguese follows Brazilian usage and Hindi uses lakh and crore.

Frequently asked questions

How large a number can it spell out?

Up to 15 digits before the decimal point and up to 30 after it. Decimals are read digit by digit, so 3.14 becomes “three point one four”. Negative numbers start with “minus”.

How are separators such as 1.500 or 1,500 understood?

A single dot or comma followed by exactly three digits is read as a thousands separator when it matches the convention of the page language (a comma on English, Hindi and Arabic pages, a dot on Spanish, Portuguese and Indonesian pages), and as the decimal mark otherwise. When both appear, the last one is the decimal mark. To avoid any doubt, type the number without separators.

Why are big numbers named differently in each language?

Languages count large numbers differently. English and Indonesian use the short scale (a billion or miliar is 1,000,000,000). Spanish uses the long scale, so 1,000,000,000 is “mil millones” and a billón is 1,000,000,000,000. Portuguese follows Brazilian usage, where a bilhão is 1,000,000,000. Hindi uses the Indian system, with lakh (100,000) and crore (10,000,000).

Does the currency or unit word change for singular and plural?

No. The word is added exactly as you type it, after the number, so type the form you need, for example “dollar” for 1 and “dollars” for 2.

Is my data uploaded or stored?

No. The tool runs in your browser, so what you enter stays on your device and is not stored by us. The only exception is the standard server log kept by the hosting provider, described in the Privacy Policy.
